sections.h2: Where is Rowlett and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Rowlett is a lakeside city of about 22 square miles in the Dallas area, mostly in Dallas County with a western edge of Rockwall County. Dalrock Road is the county dividing line, so the county that handles your taxes depends on which side of that road your house sits on.

The city says Lake Ray Hubbard, a water reservoir and recreational lake, surrounds it on two sides. The area was first settled in the 1840s, a post office opened in 1880 under the name Morris, and the name changed to Rowlett after Rowlett Creek. The Greenville and Dallas Railroad arrived in 1889, and the Bankhead Highway reached town in 1921. Rowlett incorporated in 1952 by a vote of 84 citizens.

The city says the lake's completion in 1971 made Rowlett a lakefront community, and that population grew from 5,100 in 1978 to about 64,000. For a seller, lake access and the lake's edge on two sides shape buyer interest, and a house near the shoreline may have different insurance and survey questions than one inland.

sections.h2: What are your options for a fast sale in Rowlett?
sections.html:
Three paths cover most situations: an agent listing, a cash buyer, or an investor who plans repairs. Choose by how soon you need to close and how much work the house needs.

  • A listing can bring the highest price when the house is in showing condition and you can wait for financing and appraisal.
  • A cash buyer can close on a date you choose, but expect a lower price than a polished listing.
  • An investor purchase fits houses with rental history, code issues or a tenant who cannot move out quickly.

Get at least two written offers and check who pays closing costs. If the house has been a rental, read the next section, because Rowlett registers rentals and inspects them.

sections.h2: Does Rowlett regulate rental houses, and does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. Rowlett requires annual registration of single-family houses and duplexes used as rentals, and inspections apply when tenants change. That matters if you are selling a house that has been rented, since a buyer may ask whether it is registered and current.

  • Annual registration is $50.00 per property.
  • An inspection is required at each tenant change, and the new tenant cannot move in until it passes. The inspection fee is $75.00.
  • If a tenant moves in before approval, the owner is charged $200.00.
  • The water utility account must be current, and a floor plan is required with the application.

Short-term rentals are tighter. Rowlett adopted its short-term rental ordinance in April 2025, and the registration page lists a $2,000 annual application fee with permits expiring January 31. A 1,000-foot separation requirement began in August 2026 for short-term rentals, applications are first-come, and owners must file hotel occupancy tax quarterly, including zero filings. The page says platforms like Airbnb and VRBO do not collect or remit that tax for Rowlett.

If you operate a short-term rental and plan to sell, tell buyers about the permit status, because the permit is tied to the owner and the property.

sections.h2: How are Rowlett property taxes split between two counties?
sections.html:
Because Rowlett lies in Dallas and Rockwall Counties, a house is appraised by Dallas Central Appraisal District or Rockwall Central Appraisal District, depending on its location. Check your tax statement to see which district and which county tax office applies.

Dallas CAD says a residence homestead exemption requires that you own and live in the home on January 1 of the year you apply, and you cannot claim another homestead. It also allows temporary absences if you do not set up another principal residence and intend to return in under two years. Late filing is accepted up to two years after the delinquency date.

Dallas CAD also explains a tax deferral for homeowners 65 or older or disabled: payment of taxes is postponed while you own and live in the home, but it is not cancelled, and five percent interest accrues each year. When the property is sold or transferred to an estate or heirs, the taxes and interest become due. That is the item to raise with a title company, since it will be paid from proceeds.

sections.h2: What property tax dates apply when you sell in Rowlett?
sections.html:
The tax calendar is set by Texas, so it matches other cities: appraisals are as of January 1, bills go out around October 1, and tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent.

Texas property tax dates the Comptroller prints
DateWhat happens
January 1Values set and the tax lien attaches
April 30Last day for most exemption applications
May 15Last day to file most protests, or 30 days after the notice
October 1Tax bills are mailed
February 1Unpaid tax is delinquent, penalty and interest start

Source: Texas Comptroller deadlines.

The comptroller also says a waiver of penalty and interest may be requested in writing, generally within 181 days after the delinquency date, with tax paid within 21 days of learning of the delinquency.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit in Rowlett before listing?
sections.html: A permit is not needed for a sale, but past work should have been permitted. Rowlett runs an online permitting system through which permit applications and contractor registrations are submitted. Ask the city's building safety staff if you are unsure about work done on your house.

sections.h2: What if the house is in foreclosure or inherited?
sections.html:
In either case, talk to a title company early.

  • Foreclosure: Texas lenders must give a notice of sale at least 21 days before the public auction, held on the first Tuesday of a month.
  • Inherited: a will can be probated within four years of death, and a small estate affidavit covers estates of $75,000 or less excluding homestead.

The deed from an inherited house must be recorded with the county clerk where the land sits, so Rowlett houses may be recorded in Dallas or Rockwall County.

faqs.q: Which county records my Rowlett deed?
faqs.a: The county where the land sits. Most of Rowlett is in Dallas County and a western part is in Rockwall County, with Dalrock Road as the dividing line, so check your tax statement.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house before selling it?
faqs.a: Rowlett requires annual registration of rental single-family houses and duplexes, at $50.00 per property. If the house is currently rented, ask the city whether registration is current before you list.

faqs.q: Is a short-term rental permit transferable to a buyer?
faqs.a: Ask the city. Rowlett's page lists an annual application, a January 31 expiration and a 1,000-foot separation rule, but does not say a permit follows the sale.

faqs.q: Can I defer my taxes and then sell?
faqs.a: Yes, if you qualify as 65 or older or disabled. Dallas CAD says deferred taxes plus five percent annual interest become payable when the home is sold.

faqs.q: How long does a Rowlett cash sale take?
faqs.a: It can be as short as the time needed to clear title and record the deed. Liens, an unpaid rental registration or an inherited title can lengthen it.
